numbers.context: Taper duration to avoid rebound withdrawal

negations.phrase: never start in acute decompensated shock
negations.rule: Do not initiate HFrEF beta-blockers during acute decompensated shock

negations.phrase: second- or third-degree AV block without a pacemaker
negations.rule: Contraindicated in 2nd/3rd-degree AV block unless paced

negations.phrase: Do not give beta-blockers in second- or third-degree AV block without a pacemaker, severe symptomatic bradycardia (heart rate <50 bpm), cardiogenic shock, or overt decompensated heart failure

conditions.phrase: although selectivity is lost at high doses
conditions.rule: Beta-1 cardioselectivity is dose-dependent and lost at high doses
Start mortality-reducing HFrEF beta-blockers only when euvolaemic
High-grade AV block contraindication applies without pacemaker

highYield.fact: Subclasses: β1-selective (metoprolol, bisoprolol, atenolol, esmolol; selectivity lost at high doses), non-selective (propranolol, nadolol, timolol), α1+β (carvedilol, labetalol), ISA (pindolol, acebutolol)
HFrEF mortality benefit: bisoprolol, carvedilol, metoprolol succinate — start only once euvolaemic, never in acute decompensated shock
Esmolol ultra-short half-life 9 min for acute perioperative / aortic dissection control
Unopposed alpha-1 vasoconstriction in cocaine toxicity or untreated phaeochromocytoma
Beta-blocker overdose antidote: IV glucagon (beta-receptor-independent cAMP) + atropine + high-dose insulin
Abrupt withdrawal causes rebound tachycardia/angina; taper over 1-2 weeks
